about: Authored query pairs on IBM FIBEN for tools/sample_db_bench.py. label: 'equivalent' or 'different' under the declared keys minus 'drop' (not_null:T.c, pk:T, fk:T.c). A 'different' pair carries a witness: 'real' (the two queries already differ on the FIBEN data) or a small database (missing columns are completed with legal values) that satisfies the remaining declarations and separates them. 'sibling' names the pair it negates. FIBEN declares a primary key on every table, a foreign key on 159 columns and NOT NULL only on the primary keys; the class hierarchy of its ontology is stored as tables whose primary key is also a foreign key to the parent class (LISTEDSECURITY -> SECURITY -> FINANCIALINSTRUMENT), which most join-elimination pairs use. In the data every foreign key column of the tables below is filled except PERSON.HASPLACEOFBIRTH and MONETARYAMOUNT.HASAMOUNT, so most 'different' pairs carry a small witness database.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a listed security is a security: LISTEDSECURITYID is NOT NULL and references SECURITY's key, so every row joins exactly one parent row
pairs.left: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID, l.HASTICKERSYMBOL FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l JOIN SECURITY AS s ON l.LISTEDSECURITYID = s.SECURITYID
pairs.right: SELECT LISTEDSECURITYID, HASTICKERSYMBOL FROM LISTEDSECURITY

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key a listed security may have no security row
pairs.left: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID, l.HASTICKERSYMBOL FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l JOIN SECURITY AS s ON l.LISTEDSECURITYID = s.SECURITYID
pairs.right: SELECT LISTEDSECURITYID, HASTICKERSYMBOL FROM LISTEDSECURITY

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without SECURITY's key two security rows may share an id, and the join repeats the listed security
pairs.left: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID, l.HASTICKERSYMBOL FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l JOIN SECURITY AS s ON l.LISTEDSECURITYID = s.SECURITYID
pairs.right: SELECT LISTEDSECURITYID, HASTICKERSYMBOL FROM LISTEDSECURITY

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: the join is on a monetary-amount id, not on the hierarchy key: it keeps only listed securities whose last traded value happens to be a security id
pairs.left: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l JOIN SECURITY AS s ON l.HASLASTTRADEDVALUE = s.SECURITYID
pairs.right: SELECT LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: LISTEDSECURITY, SECURITY and FINANCIALINSTRUMENT form a chain of NOT NULL keys that are also foreign keys: both joins are redundant
pairs.left: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID, l.HASLEGALNAME FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l JOIN SECURITY AS s ON l.LISTEDSECURITYID = s.SECURITYID JOIN FINANCIALINSTRUMENT AS f ON s.SECURITYID = f.FINANCIALINSTRUMENTID
pairs.right: SELECT LISTEDSECURITYID, HASLEGALNAME FROM LISTEDSECURITY

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key from SECURITY to FINANCIALINSTRUMENT a security may have no instrument row, which the second join then drops
pairs.left: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID, l.HASLEGALNAME FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l JOIN SECURITY AS s ON l.LISTEDSECURITYID = s.SECURITYID JOIN FINANCIALINSTRUMENT AS f ON s.SECURITYID = f.FINANCIALINSTRUMENTID
pairs.right: SELECT LISTEDSECURITYID, HASLEGALNAME FROM LISTEDSECURITY

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a person is an autonomous agent: PERSONID is NOT NULL and references AUTONOMOUSAGENT's key
pairs.left: SELECT p.PERSONID, p.HASLASTNAME FROM PERSON AS p JOIN AUTONOMOUSAGENT AS a ON p.PERSONID = a.AUTONOMOUSAGENTID
pairs.right: SELECT PERSONID, HASLASTNAME FROM PERSON

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without AUTONOMOUSAGENT's key an agent id may appear twice, and the join repeats the person
pairs.left: SELECT p.PERSONID, p.HASLASTNAME FROM PERSON AS p JOIN AUTONOMOUSAGENT AS a ON p.PERSONID = a.AUTONOMOUSAGENTID
pairs.right: SELECT PERSONID, HASLASTNAME FROM PERSON

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: an e-mail address is a virtual address: the same hierarchy foreign key
pairs.left: SELECT e.EMAILADDRESSID, e.HASVALUE FROM EMAILADDRESS AS e JOIN VIRTUALADDRESS AS v ON e.EMAILADDRESSID = v.VIRTUALADDRESSID
pairs.right: SELECT EMAILADDRESSID, HASVALUE FROM EMAILADDRESS

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: revenue is an element of a financial statement, which is an element of a financial report: two redundant joins along the hierarchy
pairs.left: SELECT r.REVENUEID, r.HASNAME FROM REVENUE AS r JOIN ELEMENTOFFINANCIALSTATEMENT AS e ON r.REVENUEID = e.ELEMENTOFFINANCIALSTATEMENTID JOIN ELEMENTSOFFINANCIALREPORT AS x ON e.ELEMENTOFFINANCIALSTATEMENTID = x.ELEMENTSOFFINANCIALREPORTID
pairs.right: SELECT REVENUEID, HASNAME FROM REVENUE

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key of ELEMENTOFFINANCIALSTATEMENT a statement element may have no report element row
pairs.left: SELECT r.REVENUEID, r.HASNAME FROM REVENUE AS r JOIN ELEMENTOFFINANCIALSTATEMENT AS e ON r.REVENUEID = e.ELEMENTOFFINANCIALSTATEMENTID JOIN ELEMENTSOFFINANCIALREPORT AS x ON e.ELEMENTOFFINANCIALSTATEMENTID = x.ELEMENTSOFFINANCIALREPORTID
pairs.right: SELECT REVENUEID, HASNAME FROM REVENUE

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: HASLASTTRADEDVALUE is a nullable foreign key: when it is not NULL the monetary amount exists and is unique, when it is NULL the join drops the row
pairs.left: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l JOIN MONETARYAMOUNT AS m ON l.HASLASTTRADEDVALUE = m.MONETARYAMOUNTID
pairs.right: SELECT LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY WHERE HASLASTTRADEDVALUE IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a listed security with no last traded value (NULL) joins nothing
pairs.left: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l JOIN MONETARYAMOUNT AS m ON l.HASLASTTRADEDVALUE = m.MONETARYAMOUNTID
pairs.right: SELECT LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key the last traded value may name a monetary amount that does not exist
pairs.left: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l JOIN MONETARYAMOUNT AS m ON l.HASLASTTRADEDVALUE = m.MONETARYAMOUNTID
pairs.right: SELECT LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY WHERE HASLASTTRADEDVALUE IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the place of birth is a nullable foreign key to COUNTRY's key
pairs.left: SELECT p.PERSONID FROM PERSON AS p JOIN COUNTRY AS c ON p.HASPLACEOFBIRTH = c.COUNTRYID
pairs.right: SELECT PERSONID FROM PERSON WHERE HASPLACEOFBIRTH IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: 100 of the 50,100 persons of the data have no place of birth and are dropped by the join
pairs.left: SELECT p.PERSONID FROM PERSON AS p JOIN COUNTRY AS c ON p.HASPLACEOFBIRTH = c.COUNTRYID
pairs.right: SELECT PERSONID FROM PERSON

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: two nullable foreign keys into the same parent: each join only needs its own column to be present
pairs.left: SELECT p.PERSONID FROM PERSON AS p JOIN COUNTRY AS b ON p.HASPLACEOFBIRTH = b.COUNTRYID JOIN COUNTRY AS c ON p.HASCITIZENSHIP = c.COUNTRYID
pairs.right: SELECT PERSONID FROM PERSON WHERE HASPLACEOFBIRTH IS NOT NULL AND HASCITIZENSHIP IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a person with a place of birth but no citizenship is dropped by the second join
pairs.left: SELECT p.PERSONID FROM PERSON AS p JOIN COUNTRY AS b ON p.HASPLACEOFBIRTH = b.COUNTRYID JOIN COUNTRY AS c ON p.HASCITIZENSHIP = c.COUNTRYID
pairs.right: SELECT PERSONID FROM PERSON WHERE HASPLACEOFBIRTH IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: REFERSTO is a nullable foreign key to LISTEDSECURITY's key
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM HOLDING AS h JOIN LISTEDSECURITY AS l ON h.REFERSTO = l.LISTEDSECURITYID
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM HOLDING WHERE REFERSTO IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a holding that refers to no security is not counted by the join
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM HOLDING AS h JOIN LISTEDSECURITY AS l ON h.REFERSTO = l.LISTEDSECURITYID
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM HOLDING

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: HOLDINGID is the primary key: no duplicates, no NULL
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT HOLDINGID) FROM HOLDING
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM HOLDING

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: many holdings refer to the same security (2,745 distinct securities in 534,473 holdings)
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT REFERSTO) FROM HOLDING
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM HOLDING

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: HOLDINGID is NOT NULL, so COUNT(column) counts every row
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(HOLDINGID) FROM HOLDING
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM HOLDING

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: REFERSTO is nullable: COUNT(column) skips a NULL
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(REFERSTO) FROM HOLDING
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM HOLDING

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: holdings per account: ISHELDBY is a foreign key to the account's key, the join only drops the NULL group
pairs.left: SELECT a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID AS account, COUNT(*) AS n FROM FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNT AS a JOIN HOLDING AS h ON h.ISHELDBY = a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID GROUP BY a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID
pairs.right: SELECT ISHELDBY AS account, COUNT(*) AS n FROM HOLDING WHERE ISHELDBY IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ISHELDBY

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: the right side keeps a group for holdings held by no account (NULL)
pairs.left: SELECT a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID AS account, COUNT(*) AS n FROM FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNT AS a JOIN HOLDING AS h ON h.ISHELDBY = a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID GROUP BY a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID
pairs.right: SELECT ISHELDBY AS account, COUNT(*) AS n FROM HOLDING GROUP BY ISHELDBY

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a HAVING on a grouping column is a WHERE
pairs.left: SELECT ISHELDBY, COUNT(*) AS n FROM HOLDING GROUP BY ISHELDBY HAVING ISHELDBY > 100
pairs.right: SELECT ISHELDBY, COUNT(*) AS n FROM HOLDING WHERE ISHELDBY > 100 GROUP BY ISHELDBY

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a group of two small holdings passes the HAVING on the total but no row passes the WHERE
pairs.left: SELECT ISHELDBY, SUM(HASCOUNT) AS total FROM HOLDING GROUP BY ISHELDBY HAVING SUM(HASCOUNT) > 10
pairs.right: SELECT ISHELDBY, SUM(HASCOUNT) AS total FROM HOLDING WHERE HASCOUNT > 10 GROUP BY ISHELDBY

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: SUM skips NULL anyway (and is NULL over no rows either way)
pairs.left: SELECT SUM(HASCOUNT) FROM HOLDING
pairs.right: SELECT SUM(HASCOUNT) FROM HOLDING WHERE HASCOUNT IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: COUNT(*) counts a row whose HASCOUNT is NULL
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM HOLDING
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM HOLDING WHERE HASCOUNT IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: MAX skips NULL
pairs.left: SELECT MAX(HASAMOUNT) FROM MONETARYAMOUNT
pairs.right: SELECT MAX(HASAMOUNT) FROM MONETARYAMOUNT WHERE HASAMOUNT IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the primary key is already unique
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY
pairs.right: SELECT LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: two listed securities may share a legal name (the data has 2,363 distinct names for 2,745 securities)
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT HASLEGALNAME FROM LISTEDSECURITY
pairs.right: SELECT HASLEGALNAME FROM LISTEDSECURITY

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the key of the child is selected and the parent join is on its key: every output row is unique
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT l.LISTEDSECURITYID, s.ISPROVIDEDBY FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l JOIN SECURITY AS s ON l.LISTEDSECURITYID = s.SECURITYID
pairs.right: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID, s.ISPROVIDEDBY FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l JOIN SECURITY AS s ON l.LISTEDSECURITYID = s.SECURITYID

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without SECURITY's key two identical security rows make the join repeat the listed security
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT l.LISTEDSECURITYID, s.ISPROVIDEDBY FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l JOIN SECURITY AS s ON l.LISTEDSECURITYID = s.SECURITYID
pairs.right: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID, s.ISPROVIDEDBY FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l JOIN SECURITY AS s ON l.LISTEDSECURITYID = s.SECURITYID

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the issuer of a security is a nullable foreign key to the corporation's key
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT s.ISPROVIDEDBY FROM SECURITY AS s JOIN CORPORATION AS c ON s.ISPROVIDEDBY = c.CORPORATIONID
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT ISPROVIDEDBY FROM SECURITY WHERE ISPROVIDEDBY IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: GROUP BY already makes the grouping column unique
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT ISHELDBY FROM HOLDING GROUP BY ISHELDBY
pairs.right: SELECT ISHELDBY FROM HOLDING GROUP BY ISHELDBY

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: DISTINCT on one column is a GROUP BY on it
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT ISHELDBY FROM HOLDING
pairs.right: SELECT ISHELDBY FROM HOLDING GROUP BY ISHELDBY

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: an account holds many holdings
pairs.left: SELECT ISHELDBY FROM HOLDING GROUP BY ISHELDBY
pairs.right: SELECT ISHELDBY FROM HOLDING

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: both sides of the comparison are NOT NULL keys: NOT IN has no NULL trap
pairs.left: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l WHERE l.LISTEDSECURITYID NOT IN (SELECT s.SECURITYID FROM SECURITY AS s WHERE s.ISTRADEDON = 1)
pairs.right: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM SECURITY AS s WHERE s.SECURITYID = l.LISTEDSECURITYID AND s.ISTRADEDON = 1)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: REFERSTO is nullable: one holding with no security makes NOT IN unknown for every listed security
pairs.left: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l WHERE l.LISTEDSECURITYID NOT IN (SELECT h.REFERSTO FROM HOLDING AS h WHERE h.ISHELDBY = 1)
pairs.right: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM HOLDING AS h WHERE h.REFERSTO = l.LISTEDSECURITYID AND h.ISHELDBY = 1)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: both are unknown for a NULL citizenship
pairs.left: SELECT PERSONID FROM PERSON WHERE HASCITIZENSHIP <> 5
pairs.right: SELECT PERSONID FROM PERSON WHERE NOT (HASCITIZENSHIP = 5)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: IS DISTINCT FROM keeps a person with a NULL citizenship
pairs.left: SELECT PERSONID FROM PERSON WHERE HASCITIZENSHIP <> 5
pairs.right: SELECT PERSONID FROM PERSON WHERE HASCITIZENSHIP IS DISTINCT FROM 5

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: COALESCE to 0 then comparing with 0 is NULL or 0
pairs.left: SELECT PERSONID FROM PERSON WHERE COALESCE(HASCITIZENSHIP, 0) = 0
pairs.right: SELECT PERSONID FROM PERSON WHERE HASCITIZENSHIP IS NULL OR HASCITIZENSHIP = 0

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a citizenship that is the country with id 0 also passes the COALESCE
pairs.left: SELECT PERSONID FROM PERSON WHERE COALESCE(HASCITIZENSHIP, 0) = 0
pairs.right: SELECT PERSONID FROM PERSON WHERE HASCITIZENSHIP IS NULL

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: De Morgan holds in three-valued logic
pairs.left: SELECT MONETARYAMOUNTID FROM MONETARYAMOUNT WHERE NOT (HASAMOUNT > 5 AND HASCURRENCY = 1)
pairs.right: SELECT MONETARYAMOUNTID FROM MONETARYAMOUNT WHERE HASAMOUNT <= 5 OR HASCURRENCY <> 1

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: 500,000 of the 502,745 amounts of the data are NULL and satisfy neither comparison
pairs.left: SELECT MONETARYAMOUNTID FROM MONETARYAMOUNT WHERE HASAMOUNT > 5 OR HASAMOUNT <= 5
pairs.right: SELECT MONETARYAMOUNTID FROM MONETARYAMOUNT

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a comparison and its complement cover exactly the non-NULL values
pairs.left: SELECT MONETARYAMOUNTID FROM MONETARYAMOUNT WHERE HASAMOUNT > 5 OR HASAMOUNT <= 5
pairs.right: SELECT MONETARYAMOUNTID FROM MONETARYAMOUNT WHERE HASAMOUNT IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: BETWEEN is inclusive on both ends
pairs.left: SELECT MONETARYAMOUNTID FROM MONETARYAMOUNT WHERE HASAMOUNT BETWEEN 1 AND 5
pairs.right: SELECT MONETARYAMOUNTID FROM MONETARYAMOUNT WHERE HASAMOUNT >= 1 AND HASAMOUNT <= 5

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: the end points 1 and 5 belong to BETWEEN
pairs.left: SELECT MONETARYAMOUNTID FROM MONETARYAMOUNT WHERE HASAMOUNT BETWEEN 1 AND 5
pairs.right: SELECT MONETARYAMOUNTID FROM MONETARYAMOUNT WHERE HASAMOUNT > 1 AND HASAMOUNT < 5

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: an IN list over constants is a disjunction of equalities
pairs.left: SELECT HOLDINGID FROM HOLDING WHERE ISHELDBY IN (1, 2, 3)
pairs.right: SELECT HOLDINGID FROM HOLDING WHERE ISHELDBY = 1 OR ISHELDBY = 2 OR ISHELDBY = 3

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a NULL in a NOT IN list makes the predicate unknown for every other value
pairs.left: SELECT HOLDINGID FROM HOLDING WHERE ISHELDBY NOT IN (1, 2, NULL)
pairs.right: SELECT HOLDINGID FROM HOLDING WHERE ISHELDBY NOT IN (1, 2)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: UNION DISTINCT of a set with itself, the key being unique already
pairs.left: SELECT SECURITYID FROM SECURITY UNION DISTINCT SELECT SECURITYID FROM SECURITY
pairs.right: SELECT SECURITYID FROM SECURITY

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: UNION ALL keeps both copies
pairs.left: SELECT SECURITYID FROM SECURITY UNION ALL SELECT SECURITYID FROM SECURITY
pairs.right: SELECT SECURITYID FROM SECURITY

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: every listed security is a security (foreign key), so the intersection is the whole child key set
pairs.left: SELECT SECURITYID AS id FROM SECURITY INTERSECT DISTINCT SELECT LISTEDSECURITYID AS id FROM LISTEDSECURITY
pairs.right: SELECT LISTEDSECURITYID AS id FROM LISTEDSECURITY

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key a listed security may have no security row
pairs.left: SELECT SECURITYID AS id FROM SECURITY INTERSECT DISTINCT SELECT LISTEDSECURITYID AS id FROM LISTEDSECURITY
pairs.right: SELECT LISTEDSECURITYID AS id FROM LISTEDSECURITY

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: both columns are unique, NOT NULL keys: no duplicate collapse and no NULL to compare
pairs.left: SELECT SECURITYID FROM SECURITY EXCEPT DISTINCT SELECT LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY
pairs.right: SELECT s.SECURITYID FROM SECURITY AS s WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l WHERE l.LISTEDSECURITYID = s.SECURITYID)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: EXCEPT DISTINCT collapses persons sharing a citizenship, NOT EXISTS keeps them
pairs.left: SELECT HASCITIZENSHIP FROM PERSON EXCEPT DISTINCT SELECT ISDOMICILEDIN FROM CORPORATION
pairs.right: SELECT p.HASCITIZENSHIP FROM PERSON AS p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM CORPORATION AS c WHERE c.ISDOMICILEDIN = p.HASCITIZENSHIP)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the two branches split the non-NULL counts
pairs.left: SELECT HOLDINGID FROM HOLDING WHERE HASCOUNT > 10 UNION ALL SELECT HOLDINGID FROM HOLDING WHERE HASCOUNT <= 10
pairs.right: SELECT HOLDINGID FROM HOLDING WHERE HASCOUNT IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a holding of exactly 10 is in both branches
pairs.left: SELECT HOLDINGID FROM HOLDING WHERE HASCOUNT >= 10 UNION ALL SELECT HOLDINGID FROM HOLDING WHERE HASCOUNT <= 10
pairs.right: SELECT HOLDINGID FROM HOLDING WHERE HASCOUNT IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: bag union is commutative
pairs.left: SELECT PERSONID AS id FROM PERSON UNION ALL SELECT CORPORATIONID AS id FROM CORPORATION
pairs.right: SELECT CORPORATIONID AS id FROM CORPORATION UNION ALL SELECT PERSONID AS id FROM PERSON

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the subquery returns a key: the join cannot repeat a listed security
pairs.left: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l WHERE l.HASLASTTRADEDVALUE IN (SELECT m.MONETARYAMOUNTID FROM MONETARYAMOUNT AS m WHERE m.HASAMOUNT > 100)
pairs.right: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l JOIN MONETARYAMOUNT AS m ON l.HASLASTTRADEDVALUE = m.MONETARYAMOUNTID WHERE m.HASAMOUNT > 100

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a security held several times is repeated by the join
pairs.left: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l WHERE l.LISTEDSECURITYID IN (SELECT h.REFERSTO FROM HOLDING AS h)
pairs.right: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l JOIN HOLDING AS h ON h.REFERSTO = l.LISTEDSECURITYID

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: as a filter, IN and EXISTS agree even when the subquery column has NULLs
pairs.left: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM HOLDING AS h WHERE h.REFERSTO = l.LISTEDSECURITYID)
pairs.right: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l WHERE l.LISTEDSECURITYID IN (SELECT h.REFERSTO FROM HOLDING AS h)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the correlated key is unique: at most one row, NULL when none
pairs.left: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID, (SELECT m.HASAMOUNT FROM MONETARYAMOUNT AS m WHERE m.MONETARYAMOUNTID = l.HASLASTTRADEDVALUE) AS amount FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l
pairs.right: SELECT l.LISTEDSECURITYID, m.HASAMOUNT AS amount FROM LISTEDSECURITY AS l LEFT JOIN MONETARYAMOUNT AS m ON m.MONETARYAMOUNTID = l.HASLASTTRADEDVALUE

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a derived table with a filter and a projection folds into one query
pairs.left: SELECT x.id FROM (SELECT HOLDINGID AS id, HASCOUNT FROM HOLDING WHERE HASCOUNT > 5) AS x WHERE x.HASCOUNT < 100
pairs.right: SELECT HOLDINGID AS id FROM HOLDING WHERE HASCOUNT > 5 AND HASCOUNT < 100

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: the filter after a LIMIT is not the filter before it
pairs.left: SELECT x.id FROM (SELECT HOLDINGID AS id, HASCOUNT FROM HOLDING ORDER BY HOLDINGID LIMIT 1) AS x WHERE x.HASCOUNT > 5
pairs.right: SELECT HOLDINGID FROM HOLDING WHERE HASCOUNT > 5 ORDER BY HOLDINGID LIMIT 1

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the right side is joined on its key: no row is repeated, none is lost
pairs.left: SELECT s.SECURITYID FROM SECURITY AS s LEFT JOIN LISTEDSECURITY AS l ON l.LISTEDSECURITYID = s.SECURITYID
pairs.right: SELECT SECURITYID FROM SECURITY

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without LISTEDSECURITY's key a security may match several rows
pairs.left: SELECT s.SECURITYID FROM SECURITY AS s LEFT JOIN LISTEDSECURITY AS l ON l.LISTEDSECURITYID = s.SECURITYID
pairs.right: SELECT SECURITYID FROM SECURITY

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a filter that rejects the NULL-extended rows makes the outer join inner
pairs.left: SELECT a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID, h.HOLDINGID FROM FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNT AS a LEFT JOIN HOLDING AS h ON h.ISHELDBY = a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID WHERE h.HOLDINGID IS NOT NULL
pairs.right: SELECT a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID, h.HOLDINGID FROM FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNT AS a JOIN HOLDING AS h ON h.ISHELDBY = a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a condition in ON keeps the account with a NULL holding, the same condition in WHERE drops it
pairs.left: SELECT a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID, h.HOLDINGID FROM FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNT AS a LEFT JOIN HOLDING AS h ON h.ISHELDBY = a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID AND h.HASCOUNT > 5
pairs.right: SELECT a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID, h.HOLDINGID FROM FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNT AS a LEFT JOIN HOLDING AS h ON h.ISHELDBY = a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID WHERE h.HASCOUNT > 5

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the key HOLDINGID is NULL only on the NULL-extended row
pairs.left: SELECT a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID FROM FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNT AS a LEFT JOIN HOLDING AS h ON h.ISHELDBY = a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID WHERE h.HOLDINGID IS NULL
pairs.right: SELECT a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID FROM FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNT AS a WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM HOLDING AS h WHERE h.ISHELDBY = a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: REFERSTO is nullable: an account whose holding refers to nothing looks unmatched
pairs.left: SELECT a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID FROM FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNT AS a LEFT JOIN HOLDING AS h ON h.ISHELDBY = a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID WHERE h.REFERSTO IS NULL
pairs.right: SELECT a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID FROM FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNT AS a WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM HOLDING AS h WHERE h.ISHELDBY = a.FINANCIALSERVICEACCOUNTID)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: partitioning by a key makes every partition one row
pairs.left: SELECT HOLDINGID, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY HOLDINGID ORDER BY HOLDINGID) AS n FROM HOLDING
pairs.right: SELECT HOLDINGID, 1 AS n FROM HOLDING

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: an account holds several holdings, numbered 1, 2, ...
pairs.left: SELECT HOLDINGID, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ISHELDBY ORDER BY HOLDINGID) AS n FROM HOLDING
pairs.right: SELECT HOLDINGID, 1 AS n FROM HOLDING
